newsitem.title: CANADA: Northern Telecom denies newspaper report.
newsitem.headline: Northern Telecom denies newspaper report.

text.p: A newspaper report which said Lucent Technologies Inc's deal with Southwestern Bell Telephone Co replaces an existing Southwestern Bell pact with Northern Telecom Ltd is false, Nortel said on Thursday.
"This is an inaccurate article in the Wall Street Journal," said Nortel spokesman Brian Murphy.

Murphy said Nortel had had a distribution relationship with Southwestern Bell for a long time, but it was never an exclusive, formal deal involving co-branding along the lines of the Lucent arrangement. Lucent and Southwestern Bell unveiled their deal on Wednesday.

Murphy said although the Lucent-Southwestern Bell pact will involve the U.S. Baby Bell pushing Lucent equipment over other suppliers, if Nortel enterprise customers want Nortel equipment, they can still request it.

Asked if the impact would be material, Murphy responded, "No". If there is an impact on sales in the region, Nortel will try to minimize it by maintaining its relationship with other distributors, he said.
The five states covered by the Southwestern Bell-Lucent agreement are Arkansas, Kansas, Missouri, Oklahoma and Texas.

The Wall Street Journal report suggested that if Southwestern Bell parent SBC Communication Inc succeeds in its plan to merge with Pacific Telesis Group, the distribution deal could eventually be extended to include California and Nevada.
Nortel sold off sharply after market open as investors reacted negatively to the newspaper story.
The shares were down 2.45 at 92.75 on the Toronto Stock Exchange after hitting a low of 92.10 earlier. In New York, Nortel was 1-5/8 lower at 68-1/8, up from a trough of 67-3/4.
